Authors: Torres-Sospedra, J.; Montoliu, R.; Martínez-Usó, A.; Avariento, J.P.; Arnau, T.J.; Benedito-Bordonau, M.; Huerta, J.
Title: UJIIndoorLoc: A New Multi-building and Multi-floor Database for WLAN Fingerprint-based Indoor Localization Problems
Objective: Introduce a public multi-building multi-floor WiFi fingerprinting benchmark dataset
Input_Features: 520 WAP RSSI values (-104 to 0 dBm; 100 = not detected)
Metrics: Building hit rate, floor hit rate, positioning error (m)
Reported_Findings: Covered 3 buildings ~110000 m2; 19937 training + 1111 validation samples; 25 Android devices; 20+ users; established benchmark for multi-building multi-floor localization
Limitations: Limited baseline models tested; single university campus environment; no deep learning baselines
Relevance_to_Project: Core dataset paper — this IS the dataset used in our project

Title: Multitask Learning
Objective: Demonstrate that learning multiple related tasks in parallel improves generalization via shared representations
Model: Backpropagation neural networks; KNN; kernel regression
Metrics: Generalization error, test-set accuracy across multiple tasks
Reported_Findings: MTL outperformed single-task learning (STL) across multiple domains; identified mechanisms: data amplification, attention focusing, eavesdropping, representation bias
Limitations: Primarily neural network era experiments (pre-deep-learning); limited to 1990s computing scale; auxiliary task selection not fully automated
Relevance_to_Project: Foundational theory for our multitask approach — explains why shared hidden layers for building/floor/coordinate prediction should improve generalization

Authors: Torres-Sospedra, J.; Montoliu, R.; Martínez-Usó, A.; Arnau, T.J.; Avariento, J.P.; Benedito-Bordonau, M.; Huerta, J.
Title: Comprehensive Analysis of Distance and Similarity Measures for Wi-Fi Fingerprinting Indoor Positioning Systems
Objective: Systematically compare distance and similarity measures for KNN/WKNN in WiFi fingerprinting
Model: KNN and WKNN with various distance metrics (Euclidean; Manhattan; cosine; Sørensen; etc.)
Metrics: Building hit rate, floor hit rate, mean positioning error (m)
Reported_Findings: Identified optimal distance measures for fingerprint matching; confirmed WKNN superior to simple KNN; Euclidean distance remains competitive but not always optimal
Limitations: Only tested KNN/WKNN variants — no ensemble or deep learning comparison; single-dataset evaluation
Relevance_to_Project: Directly relevant as our KNN/WKNN baseline — guides choice of distance metric

Authors: Kim, K.S.; Lee, S.; Huang, K.
Title: A Scalable Deep Neural Network Architecture for Multi-Building and Multi-Floor Indoor Localization Based on Wi-Fi Fingerprinting
Objective: Propose a scalable DNN using stacked autoencoders for multi-building, multi-floor localization
Model: Stacked Autoencoder (SAE) + feed-forward DNN for hierarchical classification
Metrics: Building hit rate, floor hit rate, mean positioning error (m)
Reported_Findings: SAE-based DNN achieved near-SOTA performance on UJIIndoorLoc; single unified architecture handles multi-building/multi-floor simultaneously with reduced computational cost
Limitations: Used hierarchical classification but not formal multitask learning; SAE architecture may be outperformed by modern alternatives (CNN, transformer)
Relevance_to_Project: Directly comparable — uses same dataset; DNN approach to same prediction targets; we can compare our MTL approach against their hierarchical DNN

Title: Low-Effort Place Recognition with WiFi Fingerprints Using Deep Learning
Objective: Apply deep neural networks to WiFi fingerprint-based building and floor recognition
Metrics: Building classification accuracy, floor classification accuracy
Reported_Findings: Demonstrated DNN can achieve high building and floor recognition accuracy with minimal feature engineering on UJIIndoorLoc
Limitations: Focused on classification only (building, floor) — did not predict coordinates; relatively simple DNN architecture
Relevance_to_Project: Comparable DNN baseline for building/floor classification; our project extends to coordinate regression via multitask learning

Title: An Overview of Multi-Task Learning in Deep Neural Networks
Objective: Survey and systematize approaches to multitask learning in deep neural networks
Model: Hard parameter sharing; soft parameter sharing; cross-stitch networks; sluice networks
Reported_Findings: Categorized MTL into hard/soft parameter sharing; explained why MTL works (data amplification, attention focusing, eavesdropping, representation bias, regularization); discussed loss weighting strategies
Limitations: Survey paper — no new experimental results; pre-dates some recent MTL advances (e.g. GradNorm)
Relevance_to_Project: Key theoretical reference for our MTL architecture design — guides hard vs soft sharing and loss balancing decisions

Authors: Chen, Z.; Badrinarayanan, V.; Lee, C.-Y.; Rabinovich, A.
Title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
Objective: Propose GradNorm, a gradient-based method to dynamically balance loss weights in MTL
Prediction_Targets: Multiple tasks with different loss scales
Model: MTL networks with GradNorm loss balancing
Reported_Findings: GradNorm significantly outperformed manual/fixed loss weighting and uncertainty-based weighting across domains
Limitations: Requires extra gradient computation per training step; hyperparameter α needs tuning; evaluated on vision tasks, not WiFi localization
Relevance_to_Project: Relevant for loss weighting strategy — our combined classification + regression MTL loss may benefit from adaptive balancing. [NEEDS VERIFICATION: applicability to WiFi domain not demonstrated in original paper]

Authors: Song, X.; Fan, X.; He, X.; Xiang, C.; Ye, Q.; Liu, L.; Wang, Z.; Yang, N.; Fang, G.
Title: A Novel Convolutional Neural Network Based Indoor Localization Framework With WiFi Fingerprinting (CNNLoc)
Objective: Apply CNN architectures to WiFi fingerprint-based indoor localization
Input_Features: WAP RSSI values (reshaped for CNN input)
Reported_Findings: CNN-based approach achieved competitive results on UJIIndoorLoc; showed that 1D CNN can extract spatial patterns from RSSI vectors
Limitations: CNN architecture choices (kernel size, depth) not exhaustively explored; limited comparison with ensemble methods
Relevance_to_Project: Directly comparable CNN baseline on same dataset; our MTL approach could use CNN as shared backbone

Authors: Salamah, A.H.; Tamazin, M.; Sharkas, M.A.; Khedr, M.E.
Title: An Enhanced WiFi Indoor Localization System Based on Machine Learning
Objective: Apply PCA + classical ML classifiers (RF/SVM/KNN/DT) to WiFi fingerprint localization
Model: Random Forest; SVM; KNN; Decision Tree
Reported_Findings: PCA reduced computation time by up to 70% with RF; tree-based classifiers robust to RSSI noise in both static and dynamic scenarios
Limitations: Custom dataset — not UJIIndoorLoc; limited to classification (no coordinate regression); single environment tested
Relevance_to_Project: Supports our use of Random Forest as a classical ML baseline; demonstrates PCA as viable preprocessing. [NEEDS VERIFICATION: exact DOI and reported accuracy numbers]

Authors: Feng, X.; Nguyen, K.A.; Luo, Z.
Title: A Survey of Deep Learning Approaches for WiFi-Based Indoor Positioning
Venue: Journal of Information and Telecommunication, 6(2), pp. 163–216
Objective: Comprehensive survey of deep learning methods for WiFi-based indoor positioning
Dataset: N/A (survey covering multiple datasets including UJIIndoorLoc)
Model: DNNs, CNNs, RNNs, autoencoders, GANs, transfer learning
Reported_Findings: Categorized DL approaches by architecture type; identified trends toward hierarchical and multi-output models; noted UJIIndoorLoc as dominant benchmark
Limitations: Survey — no new experiments; rapid evolution of field means some covered methods already superseded
Relevance_to_Project: Comprehensive context for positioning our work within DL-based indoor localization literature
